prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single, objective “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck accident — the right attorney depends on your case facts and which lawyer best matches your needs. Here’s how to find the best Dallas lawyer for your truck-accident claim and how to pick among top candidates.

What matters in a truck-accident lawyer
- Specific truck-crash experience: trucking cases involve Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) rules, black-box data, logbooks, and commercial-insurer defense teams. Choose someone who regularly handles commercial vehicle cases.  
- Trial experience and results: look for a record of significant settlements and jury verdicts, not just insurance-scheme negotiations.  
- Resources and team: your attorney should have access to accident reconstructionists, medical experts, vocational and economic experts, and investigative resources to preserve evidence.  
- Federal and state practice: many trucking cases involve interstate carriers and federal issues; experience in both courts helps.  
- Communication and client service: responsiveness, clear explanations, and a defined point of contact matter.  
- Credentials and reputation: board certification in personal injury trial law (Texas), peer-review ratings (Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers listings, or strong client reviews are useful indicators.  
- Contingency-fee structure and costs: most personal injury lawyers work on contingency (commonly 33%–40% if the case settles or differs for trial), but confirm details and who advances litigation expenses.

Where to look for top attorneys in Dallas
- Texas State Bar (lawyer search)  
- Super Lawyers (by city and practice area)  
- Martindale-Hubbell peer-review ratings  
- Avvo / Google reviews / Better Business Bureau  
- Dallas Bar Association or local plaintiff trial lawyer groups

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many in the last 12–24 months?  
- What were examples of verdicts/settlements for cases like mine?  
- Do you try cases? When was your last jury trial?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? (partner, associate, paralegal)  
- What experts will you use and how will evidence be preserved?  
- What is your fee and who pays litigation expenses?  
- What’s the likely timeline and what outcomes are realistic?

What to bring to the first meeting
- Police report and crash photos  
- Medical records and bills, ambulance records  
- Insurance information (yours and the truck’s)  
- Truck carrier name, truck/tractor and trailer numbers, driver info if known  
- Witness names and contact info, phone/video evidence

Timing and urgency
- In Texas the statute of limitations for personal injury is generally two years from the date of injury (two years for wrongful death), so contact a lawyer promptly. Early investigation preserves critical evidence (black box, logbooks, driver phone records).

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short vetted list of Dallas trucking-law attorneys if you tell me your ZIP code and any special needs (fatality, catastrophic injury, commercial truck vs. delivery van).  
- Or give a phone/email script you can use to contact firms and compare them.

Which would you prefer?
